limitations: No Digital Macaroni hands-on test was completed.
WeWeb added native backend features in 2026, so older accounts focused only on external backends do not cover the full current product.
The live pricing calculator requires JavaScript; only official starting prices and pricing structure were used.

sources.name: WeWeb Product Hunt launch and reviews

claims.statement: WeWeb visually builds the screens and browser behavior of a web app, while allowing its own backend or outside services such as Supabase, Xano, and APIs to store data and handle server work.
Paid seats start at $20 monthly, pricing is per builder rather than app user, and custom domains or WeWeb hosting can add cost.
Paid plans support code export, GitHub sync, and self-hosting.
Design freedom, outside backend connections, and code export are repeated strengths.
Databases, sign-in, permissions, changing page data, phone layouts, and debugging create a significant learning curve even when little code is typed.
A detailed community account reports that WeWeb AI replaced working sign-in logic with sample data, illustrating why generated changes need review but not establishing a normal result.

scoreRationale.onboarding: The canvas is approachable, but a real app quickly requires technical concepts.
scoreRationale.product: WeWeb offers strong screen design, data connections, and an exit through code export.
scoreRationale.support: Review-platform support scores are positive, while community troubleshooting can still be difficult outside common paths.
scoreRationale.billing: The $20 seat start and unlimited app users are attractive, but backend, hosting, and more builders must be counted.
scoreRationale.overall: WeWeb suits a technically curious builder who wants more control than a template tool without writing every screen from scratch.

conflictsAndUnknowns: WeWeb is called no-code, yet reliable apps still require a developer-like understanding of data and security.
The product changed in 2026 with native backend work, so older external-backend accounts cover only one setup.
No hands-on auth, export, speed, or phone-layout test was completed.
